structured_output.world_model: W6: time is about 0.1 s plus steps times per-step cost. Time noise is about ±0.04 s. Accuracy rises slowly with optimizer steps, at about 1.5-2 s/pp. The tip's population mean is about 0.752, and 3-seed noise is about 0.2 pp. Backward truncation and memory-bound savings beat their MAC share. Non-systems tweaks are null or negative. Systems-only changes give 1-2%. Seeds 0-2 in a new build are mostly a re-roll around 0.752.

forecasts.reason: +0.25 epoch is about +2.6% steps, so time rises about 0.1 s. The accuracy gain of about 0.1 pp is below noise.
The group-2 freeze saves about 0.24 s and the top-up costs about 0.1 s, so net time is about 2.5% below E036. Accuracy is roughly neutral within noise.
The saving is at most 1-2% of the 135 ms of non-step work. It is hard to separate from drift, and kernel reselection can move accuracy.
An extra conv on tiny maps adds about 2% time including BN and launch overhead. The accuracy gain is uncertain, probably about +0.1 pp.
ReLU saves some memory traffic, so time falls by about 1-3%. Accuracy likely drops a little because the recipe is tuned for GELU.

cruxes: Is the tip's true unselected population mean about 0.752 or about 0.7535? This sets whether any further time cut is feasible at the official 40-seed bar.
Does the group-2 freeze keep its time saving when combined with an epoch top-up, and is its accuracy cost under 0.1 pp in a same-build pairing?
How much of the remaining step time is memory-bound elementwise work, which activation or layer changes could remove?
